text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Elevated SRV lookup error rate detected for service 'api-gateway' in eu-central-1b. 5xx from internal name resolution (CoreDNS) observed across multiple clusters. Error rate jumped ~40% at 03:05 UTC. Paging oncall. Metrics: https://metrics.internal.example.com/alerts/1719904321

emma_oncall: ack -- I'm on it. Pulling logs and cluster view now.

raj_infra: I'm connected to eu-central-1b cluster. Seeing repeated timeouts from coredns to kube-proxy for SRV lookups. CoreDNS pods are Restarting (OOMKilled) on two nodes. Logs show a lot of SERVFAIL and i/o timeouts.

sasha_runtime: copying useful logs:
```
2026-03-08T03:06:12Z core-dns[pid]: lookup api-backend._tcp.default.svc.cluster.local. from 10.128.0.5:53: i/o timeout
2026-03-08T03:06:13Z core-dns[pid]: health check failed: forward: dial tcp 10.0.2.11:53: i/o timeout
```

raj_infra: `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide --context=cluster-eu-central-1b` shows CoreDNS on nodes node-azb-01 and node-azb-03 flapping. Node network stats show rx errors.

liu_network: I started a quick traceroute from node-azb-01 to the cluster DNS service IP and to the forwarding resolver; packet loss starts after the AZ transit hop: `* * *` at hop 5. Escalating to carrier. Opening ticket with provider.

emma_oncall: Can we route around the affected AZ? We need customer-impact mitigation first. alex_support, any user-visible incidents?

alex_support: We have ~12 active support tickets referencing 503s for webhook delivery and a few customers reported degraded API latency in eu-central. Severity is limited but trending. I'm drafting a status note for impacted customers: "temporary service degradation for eu-central-1b - engineering investigating".

sasha_runtime: Quick mitigation plan: 1) scale coredns replicas in eu-central-1b to reduce individual pod pressure, 2) temporarily update service discovery routing to deprioritize instances in eu-central-1b (consul/traffic router), 3) add fallback DNS forwarders to node-local config so pods can use node-local cache instead of the flapping cores. I'll run the commands.

raj_infra: executing step 1: `kubectl --context=cluster-eu-central-1b -n kube-system scale deploy/coredns --replicas=5`

deploy-bot: Deploy started: scale/coredns -> 5 replicas (eu-central-1b). CI job 89234 kicked.

sasha_runtime: patching kube-proxy/node-local-dns: adding fallback IPs (10.0.1.8, 10.0.1.9) which are healthy resolvers in eu-central-1a/c. Command:
```
kubectl --context=cluster-eu-central-1b -n kube-system patch cm node-local-dns --type merge -p '{"data":{"upstreamNameservers":"10.0.1.8 10.0.1.9"}}'
```

raj_infra: Also reducing weight for eu-central-1b in our internal traffic router (consul): `consul services update-weight api-gateway --region eu --az eu-central-1b --weight 10` (was 50). Should shift new traffic away from azb.

liu_network: Provider responded: they see intermittent fiber error affecting east-west AZ transit in eu-central-1 (their config shows packet drops between fabric switches). They're applying a BGP path change and monitoring. ETA for stabilizing link: ~18-45 minutes.

emma_oncall: Good. Monitoring customer tickets and metrics. Sasha/Raj, what about persistent config changes? We should avoid manual long-term patches here. Keep changes reversible and document.

sasha_runtime: Agreed — all changes are reversible. Rolling back will be simple: scale to original replicas and remove fallback upstreams once link healthy. Also I added a temporary CoreDNS health plugin tweak to fail faster so endpoints are marked unhealthy sooner to avoid retries: patched config map with `max_fails 2`.

raj_infra: After scaling and consul weight change we see SRV error rate drop from 40% -> 12% over the last 4 minutes. Pod restarts on CoreDNS reduced as well.

alex_support: Noting customer impact update: "We've reduced traffic through the affected AZ and applied temporary fixes. Engineers are monitoring. No data loss expected. Follow-up postmortem will be shared." Posting to status page now.

emma_oncall: Handing off to night-shift oncall @raj_infra at 03:25 UTC. I'll stay available for questions. Raj, please summarize actions and keep monitoring until provider confirms stable.

raj_infra: Handoff ack. Summary: 1) scaled CoreDNS to 5 replicas in eu-central-1b, 2) added node-local fallback upstreams (10.0.1.8/9), 3) reduced consul weight for eu-central-1b to 10, 4) patched CoreDNS config to reduce retries. Provider working on BGP reroute. Monitoring shows improvements. Will watch for 30m window.

liu_network: Provider applied path change at 03:32 UTC and packet loss dropped to negligible by 03:36 UTC. Still watching.

sasha_runtime: Rolling back the max_fails patch to default now that upstream looks stable. Command executed.

deploy-bot: ConfigMap patch and deployment updates completed. All jobs passed.

raj_infra: Restoring consul weights to baseline (50) for eu-central-1b at 03:44 UTC after sustained healthy metrics. `consul services update-weight api-gateway --region eu --az eu-central-1b --weight 50`

emma_oncall: Closing the page. We'll open a follow-up postmortem for RCA: suspected provider fiber flaps causing inter-AZ network packet loss, which led to CoreDNS forwarder timeouts and SRV lookup failures. Action items: 1) add more cross-AZ resilient forwarders, 2) improve alert triggers to include node-level network rx errors, 3) run chaos test for AZ-failure scenarios on service discovery. Assigning owners: sasha_runtime (1), raj_infra (2), liu_network (3).

alex_support: I'll update customers with resolution note and link to postmortem when available.

emma_oncall: last check at 03:45 UTC — metrics stable, support counts decreasing. Closing thread and incident. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
